quests.conceptTitle: Cause & Result: Because Of / So / Since
quests.sentence: The flight was delayed because of a mechanical issue.
quests.ruleExplanation: Because of a mechanical issue gives a reason using a noun phrase (not a full clause with a subject and verb), following the passive was delayed.
quests.nativeTip: Because of is followed directly by a noun phrase, not a full clause, to give a reason.

quests.conceptTitle: Cause & Result: Because Of / So / Since
quests.sentence: She was exhausted, so she went to bed early.
quests.ruleExplanation: So she went to bed early states the result of being exhausted, joined by a comma after the first clause.
quests.nativeTip: So introduces the result of what came before it, connected by a comma.

quests.conceptTitle: Cause & Result: Because Of / So / Since
quests.sentence: Since the roads were icy, drivers were advised to slow down.
quests.ruleExplanation: Since the roads were icy fronts the reason, followed by a comma and a passive result clause, drivers were advised to slow down.
quests.nativeTip: Since can front a reason clause too (a different use from present-perfect since), followed by a comma and the result.

quests.conceptTitle: Contrast: Although / But / Even Though
quests.sentence: Although it was raining, the game continued as scheduled.
quests.ruleExplanation: Although it was raining fronts the contrasting circumstance, followed by a comma and the game continued as scheduled, the surprising main result.
quests.nativeTip: Although fronts a contrasting idea, followed by a comma and the main clause that goes against it.

quests.conceptTitle: Contrast: Although / But / Even Though
quests.sentence: The team worked hard, but they still missed the deadline.
quests.ruleExplanation: But joins two contrasting ideas — hard work and a missed deadline — with a comma placed right before but.
quests.nativeTip: But joins two contrasting ideas mid-sentence, with a comma right before it.

quests.conceptTitle: Contrast: Although / But / Even Though
quests.sentence: Even though the proposal was well researched, it lacked a clear budget.
quests.ruleExplanation: Even though the proposal was well researched fronts the contrast, followed by a comma and it lacked a clear budget, the surprising shortfall.
quests.nativeTip: Even though works like although, fronting the contrast before a comma and the main clause.

quests.conceptTitle: Passive Voice Inside a Relative Clause
quests.sentence: The bridge that was built last century is still in use.
quests.ruleExplanation: That was built last century combines a defining relative clause with the passive voice, describing which bridge is still in use.
quests.nativeTip: A passive relative clause (was built) can describe the noun the same way an active one would.

quests.conceptTitle: Passive Voice Inside a Relative Clause
quests.sentence: The memo which was submitted yesterday contained several errors.
quests.ruleExplanation: Which was submitted yesterday combines which with the passive voice, describing exactly which report contained the errors.
quests.nativeTip: Which can also introduce a passive relative clause, describing the noun that received the action.

quests.conceptTitle: Passive Voice Inside a Relative Clause
quests.sentence: The employees who were laid off received severance packages.
quests.ruleExplanation: Who were laid off combines who with the passive voice, describing employees who had the action of laying off done to them.
quests.nativeTip: Who plus a passive verb describes people who had something done to them.

quests.conceptTitle: Conditional with an Embedded Relative Clause
quests.sentence: If the candidate who impressed us accepts our offer, we will celebrate.
quests.ruleExplanation: Who impressed us describes candidate right inside the if-clause, before the condition accepts the offer continues and the comma introduces the main clause.
quests.nativeTip: A relative clause can sit inside the if-clause, describing the noun before the condition continues.

quests.conceptTitle: Conditional with an Embedded Relative Clause
quests.sentence: Unless the vendor who supplies our materials responds soon, we will switch suppliers.
quests.ruleExplanation: Who supplies our materials describes vendor inside the unless-clause, before the condition responds soon continues.
quests.nativeTip: The same embedding works with unless — a relative clause describes the noun inside the condition.

quests.conceptTitle: Conditional with an Embedded Relative Clause
quests.sentence: If she finds a job that pays well, she will relocate.
quests.ruleExplanation: That pays well describes job inside the if-clause, adding detail before the condition and the comma leading to the main clause.
quests.nativeTip: A that-clause can describe the noun inside the if-clause the same way.

quests.conceptTitle: Reported Speech with an Embedded Relative Clause
quests.sentence: She said that the man who called earlier was her supplier.
quests.ruleExplanation: Who called earlier describes man inside the that-clause, adding identifying detail within the reported statement.
quests.nativeTip: A relative clause can describe a noun inside a reported statement, adding detail about who is being talked about.

quests.conceptTitle: Reported Speech with an Embedded Relative Clause
quests.sentence: He mentioned that the project which he led had succeeded.
quests.ruleExplanation: Which he led describes project inside the that-clause, adding detail before the backshifted verb had succeeded.
quests.nativeTip: Which can describe a noun inside a reported clause the same way.

quests.conceptTitle: Reported Speech with an Embedded Relative Clause
quests.sentence: They explained that the policy that changed affected everyone.
quests.ruleExplanation: That changed uses that as a relative pronoun describing policy, nested inside the larger that-clause introduced by explained.
quests.nativeTip: That can serve two jobs at once here: introducing the reported clause, and then again as the relative pronoun inside it.

quests.conceptTitle: Modal Passive with a Time Clause
quests.sentence: The report must be submitted before the committee meets.
quests.ruleExplanation: Must be submitted (modal passive) pairs with before the committee meets, a present-tense time clause even though it refers to the future.
quests.nativeTip: A modal passive main clause pairs with a simple present time clause introduced by before.

quests.conceptTitle: Modal Passive with a Time Clause
quests.sentence: The system should be updated after the new version is released.
quests.ruleExplanation: Should be updated (modal passive) pairs with after the new version is released, a present-tense passive time clause.
quests.nativeTip: The same modal-passive-plus-time-clause pattern applies with after and a present-tense passive clause.

quests.conceptTitle: Modal Passive with a Time Clause
quests.sentence: The results can be reviewed once the audit is complete.
quests.ruleExplanation: Can be reviewed (modal passive) pairs with once the audit is complete, a present-tense time clause signaling a future condition.
quests.nativeTip: Once introduces a time clause the same way before and after do, still in present tense.

quests.conceptTitle: Conditional with Passive Voice
quests.sentence: If the deadline is missed, the contract will be terminated.
quests.ruleExplanation: If the deadline is missed fronts a passive condition, followed by a comma and the contract will be terminated, a passive result.
quests.nativeTip: A passive if-clause can front the sentence, followed by a comma and a passive will-result.

quests.conceptTitle: Conditional with Passive Voice
quests.sentence: Unless the errors are corrected, the report will be rejected.
quests.ruleExplanation: Unless the errors are corrected fronts a passive condition, followed by a comma and the report will be rejected, a passive result.
quests.nativeTip: Unless can front a passive condition too, followed by a comma and a passive result.

quests.conceptTitle: Conditional with Passive Voice
quests.sentence: If more funding were provided, the project would be completed faster.
quests.ruleExplanation: If more funding were provided uses hypothetical past-tense passive, paired with the project would be completed faster, a hypothetical passive result.
quests.nativeTip: A hypothetical passive if-clause (were provided) pairs with a passive would-result.

quests.conceptTitle: Multi-Clause Mastery: Contrast + Cause/Result
quests.sentence: Although sales increased, profits fell because costs rose sharply.
quests.ruleExplanation: Although sales increased sets up a contrast, and because costs rose sharply explains why profits still fell — two connectors doing two different jobs in one sentence.
quests.nativeTip: Combine although (contrast) with because (reason) in one sentence, each connecting a different pair of ideas.

quests.conceptTitle: Multi-Clause Mastery: Contrast + Cause/Result
quests.sentence: Because the market shifted, many companies struggled, but some adapted quickly.
quests.ruleExplanation: Because the market shifted fronts the reason, many companies struggled states one result, and but some adapted quickly adds a contrasting second result.
quests.nativeTip: Combine a fronted because-clause with a mid-sentence but, joining three ideas in sequence.

quests.conceptTitle: Multi-Clause Mastery: Contrast + Cause/Result
quests.sentence: Even though the budget was tight, our team delivered this project on time.
quests.ruleExplanation: Even though the budget was tight fronts the contrast, followed by a comma and our team delivered the project on time, the successful result despite that constraint.
quests.nativeTip: Combine even though (contrast) with a simple result clause, reviewing the fronted-contrast pattern from earlier.

quests.conceptTitle: Reported Speech with an Embedded Conditional
quests.sentence: She said that if the weather improved, they would leave early.
quests.ruleExplanation: If the weather improved fronts a hypothetical condition inside the larger that-clause, followed by its own comma before they would leave early.
quests.nativeTip: A fronted if-clause can sit inside a reported statement, with its own internal comma.

quests.conceptTitle: Reported Speech with an Embedded Conditional
quests.sentence: He mentioned that unless the price dropped, he wouldn't buy it.
quests.ruleExplanation: Unless the price dropped fronts a condition inside the that-clause, followed by its own comma before he wouldn't buy it.
quests.nativeTip: An unless-clause can be embedded the same way inside a reported statement.

quests.conceptTitle: Reported Speech with an Embedded Conditional
quests.sentence: They explained that if the flight was delayed, they would miss their connection.
quests.ruleExplanation: If the flight was delayed fronts a passive condition inside the that-clause, followed by its own comma before they would miss the connection.
quests.nativeTip: A passive if-clause can be embedded inside a reported statement too.

quests.conceptTitle: Full Mastery: Multi-System Integration
quests.sentence: Although the proposal that she submitted was rejected, she remained confident about her next attempt.
quests.ruleExplanation: Although the proposal that she submitted was rejected layers a relative clause (that she submitted) and a passive verb (was rejected) inside a fronted contrast clause, before the comma and main clause.
quests.nativeTip: Combine a fronted contrast clause with a relative clause and a passive verb, all in one sentence.

quests.conceptTitle: Full Mastery: Multi-System Integration
quests.sentence: If the manager who reviewed our application approves it, the funding will be released next month.
quests.ruleExplanation: If the manager who reviewed our application approves it nests a relative clause (who reviewed our application) inside the if-clause, and the funding will be released next month gives a passive future result.
quests.nativeTip: Combine a conditional, a relative clause, and a passive result, layering three systems into one sentence.

quests.conceptTitle: Full Mastery: Multi-System Integration
quests.sentence: She explained that although the flight had been delayed, the passengers who were waiting remained calm.
quests.ruleExplanation: She explained that although the flight had been delayed frames a contrast (although) and past perfect passive (had been delayed) inside a reported statement, and the passengers who were waiting remained calm adds a relative clause describing the passengers, closing the curriculum with its most integrated sentence.
quests.nativeTip: Combine reported speech, a contrast clause, past perfect passive, and a relative clause — four systems in one final sentence.
